name: Vegetable Korma
subtitle: mixed vegetables in a mild coconut and cashew gravy, southern style
prepNotes: The southern korma leans on coconut rather than cream, and on fennel rather than garam masala. It should taste sweet and aromatic, not rich.
Add the thick coconut milk off the heat. Boiled coconut milk separates into oil and grit.

steps.text: Blend the grated coconut, cashews, fennel and a little water to a fine paste.
steps.tip: Fine. Any grit here stays gritty in the finished dish.

steps.text: Fry the whole spices and curry leaves in coconut oil, then the onion until soft but not brown.
steps.tip: Not brown. This gravy should stay pale.

steps.text: Add ginger, garlic and green chilli, then the vegetables and enough hot water to barely cover.
Simmer covered until the vegetables are just tender, about 12 minutes.
Stir in the coconut-cashew paste and cook 5 minutes until it thickens.
Take off the heat, stir in the thick coconut milk, and check the salt.
steps.tip: Off the heat. This is the step people get wrong.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat very gently; coconut milk splits on a hard boil. Not suitable for freezing.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
